title: The PCP Exam, Part 1: Vital Signs, Head, Neck and Chest
next: Chapter 16, Lesson 2: The heart, abdomen, limbs and nervous system

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already take vital signs and check patients head to toe with DCAP-BTLS. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Use the exam techniques and read vital signs as a trend
  2. Read the head, eyes, neck and skin for clues to the cause
  3. Do a full chest exam and let it drive PCP decisions like CPAP

Textbook: Chapter 16, from Examination Techniques (PDF p. 1357) to the Chest exam
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already take vital signs and check patients from head to toe for deformities, bruises, wounds and swelling. So today isn't about starting over; it's about going deeper. As a PCP, your exam has a new job: it has to point to a cause, a working diagnosis, and then to a protocol, and sometimes a drug. We'll cover three things: the exam techniques and how to read vital signs as a trend; what the head, eyes, neck and skin can tell you; and a full chest exam, including how your findings decide whether CPAP is right.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经会测生命体征，也会从头到脚检查畸形、瘀伤、伤口和肿胀。所以今天不是从零开始，而是往深处走。作为 PCP，你的体检多了一项任务：它要指向病因，也就是工作诊断，再指向一个流程，有时还指向一种药。今天讲三件事：检查手法，以及怎样把生命体征当作趋势来读；头、眼、颈和皮肤能告诉你什么；以及完整的胸部检查，包括你的发现如何决定该不该上 CPAP。

slides.title: Four techniques, used on purpose
slides.body:
TechniqueWhat you're after
InspectThe whole patient first, then each region
PalpateTenderness, crepitus, masses, pulses, skin temperature
PercussAir (hyperresonant) vs blood or fluid (dull)
AuscultateBreath, heart and bowel sounds

Stethoscope: the bell rests lightly for low sounds; the diaphragm presses firmly for high sounds.
slides.say: You know the four techniques: inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation. As a PCP, use them on purpose. Inspection starts at the door with the whole patient, then goes region by region. Palpation finds tenderness, crepitus, a crackling or grating feeling, masses, pulses and skin temperature. Percussion means tapping and listening to the note: over the chest, a hollow, booming note suggests too much air, and a dull note suggests fluid or blood. For auscultation, the bell rests lightly and picks up low sounds, and the diaphragm presses firmly and picks up high sounds, like breath and bowel sounds.
slides.sayZh: 四种手法你都知道：视诊、触诊、叩诊、听诊。作为 PCP，要有目的地用。视诊从进门看整个病人开始，再逐个部位看。触诊找压痛、捻发音（一种噼啪或摩擦感）、肿块、脉搏和皮温。叩诊就是敲一敲、听声音：胸部敲出空空的、轰响的声音提示气太多，敲出发闷的声音提示有液体或血。听诊时，钟型件轻贴，听低调音；膜型件压紧，听高调音，比如呼吸音和肠鸣音。

slides.title: Vital signs are a trend
slides.body:
One set is a photo. Serial sets are a movie.

  • First set = baseline; compare every later set with it
  • Pulse: rate, rhythm, quality; count 15 s × 4
  • Unresponsive: confirm a central pulse, count the most distal one
  • Under 1 year: brachial pulse
  • Breathing: 30 s × 2, while you still seem to feel the pulse
slides.say: Here's a mindset shift. One set of vital signs is a photo; several sets over time are a movie, and the movie shows where your patient is heading. The first set is your baseline, and every later set is compared with it. Count the pulse for fifteen seconds times four. In an unresponsive patient, confirm a central pulse, then count the most distal pulse you can feel, because that gives you a rough idea of the pressure. In babies under one, use the brachial pulse. Count breathing for thirty seconds times two, while you still seem to be feeling the pulse.
slides.sayZh: 先换个思路：一组生命体征是一张照片，隔一段时间测的多组是一段视频，视频才看得出病人往哪个方向走。第一组是基线，之后每一组都和它比。脉搏数十五秒乘四。无反应的病人先确认中心脉搏，再数能摸到的最远端的脉搏，这样能粗估血压。一岁以下婴儿摸肱动脉。呼吸数三十秒乘二，数的时候装作还在摸脉。

slides.title: Breathing patterns point to a cause
slides.body:
PatternLooks likeThink of
Biot (ataxic)Totally irregular, with pausesRaised intracranial pressure
Cheyne-StokesBuilds up, fades, then pausesBrainstem injury
KussmaulDeep, gaspingDiabetic ketoacidosis
TachypneaFast and shallowLung disease, anxiety, heart failure

Also look for tripod position, accessory muscles and retractions.
slides.say: The pattern of breathing can point to a cause. Biot, or ataxic, breathing is totally irregular, with pauses; think raised pressure inside the skull. Cheyne-Stokes breathing builds up, fades away, then pauses, and it's linked to brainstem injury. Kussmaul breathing is deep and gasping, classic for diabetic ketoacidosis, or DKA, a dangerous high-sugar state. Tachypnea, fast shallow breathing, has many causes, from anxiety to asthma to heart failure. For a PCP, a pattern is a clue to act on: Kussmaul breathing means check the glucose, and Biot breathing after a head injury makes this a time-critical call.
slides.sayZh: 呼吸的样子能指向病因。Biot 呼吸，又叫共济失调性呼吸，完全没有规律、夹着停顿，要想到颅内压升高。潮式呼吸（Cheyne-Stokes）先渐渐加深加快、再渐渐变弱、然后停一下，和脑干损伤有关。Kussmaul 呼吸深大、像在喘，是糖尿病酮症酸中毒（DKA，一种危险的高血糖状态）的典型表现。呼吸急促就是又快又浅，原因很多，从焦虑、哮喘到心衰都有。对 PCP 来说，呼吸型是要据此行动的线索：看到 Kussmaul 呼吸就测血糖；头部受伤后出现 Biot 呼吸，这就是分秒必争的病人。

slides.title: Blood pressure: get a true number
slides.body:
• BP = cardiac output × vascular resistance
  • Low diastolic = less blood to the heart muscle
  • Cuff covers ½ to ⅔ of the upper arm
  • Too small or tight → falsely high; too big or loose → falsely low
  • Avoid: injured arm, dialysis fistula, mastectomy side
  • Pain and fear raise BP: judge the trend

SpO₂ can mislead too: cold or hypotensive patient, CO poisoning, motion.
slides.say: Blood pressure deserves extra care now, because some of your drug decisions depend on it. Blood pressure equals cardiac output times vascular resistance, and the diastolic matters too: the coronary arteries fill between beats, so a low diastolic means less blood to the heart muscle. The cuff should cover one half to two thirds of the upper arm. Too small or too tight reads falsely high; too big or too loose reads falsely low. Avoid an injured arm, a dialysis fistula, and the side of a mastectomy. And watch the trend, because pain and fear push the pressure up.
slides.sayZh: 现在测血压要更用心，因为你的一些用药决定取决于它。血压等于心输出量乘以血管阻力；舒张压也重要：冠状动脉在两次心跳之间灌注，舒张压低就意味着心肌得到的血少。袖带应覆盖上臂的二分之一到三分之二。太小或太紧，读数假性偏高；太大或太松，读数假性偏低。避开受伤的手臂、有透析瘘管的手臂和做过乳房切除的一侧。还要看趋势，因为疼痛和恐惧会把血压推高。

slides.q: A small, thin woman has chest pain. Your partner used a large adult cuff and got 104/68. Nitroglycerin is next in your plan. What do you do?
options: Withhold nitroglycerin for the rest of the call
Recheck with a cuff that fits, then decide
Give it: a large cuff reads falsely high
Give half a dose to be safe
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A small, thin woman has chest pain. Your partner used a large adult cuff and got one hundred four over sixty-eight. Nitroglycerin is next in your plan. What do you do? A, withhold nitroglycerin for the rest of the call. B, recheck with a cuff that fits, then decide. C, give it, because a large cuff reads falsely high. D, give half a dose to be safe. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位瘦小的女性胸痛，搭档用了大号成人袖带，测得一百零四比六十八。下一步计划给硝酸甘油。你怎么做？A 本次出车全程不给硝酸甘油；B 换合适的袖带复测，再决定；C 照给，因为大袖带读数假性偏高；D 保险起见给半量。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A cuff that's too large reads falsely low, so her real systolic may be higher. BC lists a systolic under one hundred ten as a contraindication to nitroglycerin, so you need a true number before you decide. A could deny her a useful drug because of a bad reading. C has it backwards: a large cuff reads low, not high. D isn't an option: you never dose around a contraindication.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。袖带太大读数会假性偏低，她真实的收缩压可能更高。BC 把收缩压低于一百一十列为硝酸甘油的禁忌证，所以做决定前要先拿到真实的数字。A 可能因为一个错误读数让她错过有用的药；C 把方向说反了，大袖带读数偏低而不是偏高；D 不是可选项：绝不能靠减量绕开禁忌证。

slides.title: First look: impression, mind, skin
slides.body:
• Sick or not sick? Decide from the doorway
  • AO×4: person, place, time, event; AVPU = best response
  • Pale = poor perfusion; cyanosis = low O₂; mottling = prolonged shock
  • Tenting = dehydration; in older adults test the upper chest
  • Clubbed fingers = chronic lung disease
  • Check hidden skin; bruises of many ages → consider abuse
slides.say: Your exam starts before you touch anyone. From the doorway, decide: sick or not sick? Then mental status. Alert and oriented times four means the patient knows person, place, time and event, and with AVPU you record the best response you can get. Skin is a fast window on perfusion: pale means poor perfusion, blue means low oxygen, and mottling, a blotchy pattern, means shock that has lasted a while. If pinched skin stays up like a tent, think dehydration; in older adults, test the upper chest. And sort chronic from acute: clubbed fingertips mean long-term lung disease, not today's crisis.
slides.sayZh: 体检在你碰到病人之前就开始了。在门口先判断：病得重不重？然后看精神状态。清醒定向乘四，是病人知道自己是谁、在哪里、什么时间、发生了什么事；用 AVPU 时，记录你能引出的最佳反应。皮肤是看灌注最快的窗口：苍白是灌注差，发紫是缺氧，花斑（一块块的斑驳）说明休克已经持续了一段时间。捏起的皮肤像帐篷一样立着，要想到脱水；老人要在上胸部测。还要分清慢性和急性：杵状指说明长期肺病，不是今天的急症。

slides.title: Head and eyes
slides.body:
• Palpate the skull front to back: step-off, crepitus
  • Fontanelle (under 18 months): bulging at rest = ↑ pressure; sunken = dry
  • Pupils: size (mm), shape, equal, light reaction; check early if LOC ↓
  • Unequal pupils are normal in about 20% of people
  • Eye movements: follow your finger in an H
  • Vision: count fingers at 2 m, 1 m, 30 cm; record the distance
slides.say: Now the head. Feel the whole skull from front to back for a step-off, which is a sudden ledge in the bone, or crepitus. In infants under eighteen months, feel the soft spot: a bulging fontanelle in a calm baby suggests raised pressure, and a sunken one suggests dehydration. Check the pupils early in anyone with a lowered level of consciousness: size in millimetres, shape, equality and reaction to light. But about twenty percent of people have unequal pupils normally, so match it to the whole patient. Check eye movements in an H shape, and test vision by counting fingers at set distances.
slides.sayZh: 接下来是头部。从前到后摸遍整个颅骨，找台阶感（骨头上突然的高低错位）或捻发音。十八个月以下的婴儿要摸前囟：安静时前囟膨隆提示颅内压升高，凹陷提示脱水。意识水平下降的病人要尽早查瞳孔：大小（毫米）、形状、是否等大、对光反射。但大约百分之二十的人瞳孔本来就不等大，所以要结合整个病人来判断。让病人眼睛跟着手指走 H 形查眼球运动，并在固定距离数手指来测视力。

slides.title: Ears, nose, neck and C-spine
slides.body:
• Blood or clear fluid from ears/nose after trauma → skull base fracture
  • Battle sign: bruising behind the ear
  • JVD: record the patient's angle and how high it rises
  • Trachea midline? Check, but don't spend long
  • C-spine: midline bony tenderness = worry; sides = usually muscle
  • Pain or tingling with movement → stop, protect the spine
slides.say: After head trauma, blood or clear fluid from the ears or nose suggests a fracture at the base of the skull, and so does bruising behind the ear, called Battle sign. In the neck, look for jugular venous distention, or JVD: swollen neck veins. Record it like a PCP: the patient's angle, and how far up the neck it rises. Check quickly that the trachea is midline. For the cervical spine, tenderness over the bony midline at the back is a worry; tenderness at the sides is usually muscle. If any movement causes pain or tingling, stop and protect the spine.
slides.sayZh: 头部外伤后，耳朵或鼻子流血或流清水样液体，提示颅底骨折；耳后瘀青（叫 Battle 征）也是同样的提示。颈部要看颈静脉怒张（JVD），也就是脖子上的静脉鼓起来。要像 PCP 一样记录：病人的体位角度，以及怒张沿脖子升到多高。快速确认气管居中。颈椎方面，后正中骨性部位压痛要警惕；两侧压痛通常是肌肉问题。任何动作引起疼痛或麻刺感，立即停止并保护脊柱。

slides.title: The chest exam, step by step
slides.body:
1. Expose with privacy; dress open wounds
  2. Inspect: rate, depth, symmetry, retractions, accessory muscles, scars
  3. Palpate: tenderness, crepitus, air under the skin, equal rise
  4. Percuss if possible: hyperresonant = air; dull = blood or fluid
  5. Auscultate on bare skin: one full breath per spot, mouth open
  6. Repeat on the back
slides.say: Here's a complete chest exam. Expose the chest, protecting privacy, and dress any open wound. Inspect: rate, depth, symmetry, accessory muscles, and retractions, where the skin sucks in above or between the ribs. Look for scars, too: a long midline scar means past heart surgery. Palpate for tenderness, crepitus and air under the skin, called subcutaneous emphysema, and feel whether both sides rise equally. Percuss if the scene allows. Then listen on bare skin, never through clothing, for one full breath at each spot, with the patient breathing through an open mouth. Then do the back.
slides.sayZh: 下面是一套完整的胸部检查。暴露胸部，注意保护隐私，有开放伤先包扎。视诊：频率、深度、两侧是否对称、辅助呼吸肌，还有三凹征，也就是吸气时锁骨上或肋间的皮肤往里陷。也要看疤痕：胸前正中一条长疤说明做过心脏手术。触诊找压痛、捻发音和皮下的气体（叫皮下气肿），并感受两侧起伏是否一样。现场允许就叩诊。然后直接贴着皮肤听，绝不隔着衣服，每个位置听一次完整的吸气和呼气，让病人张口呼吸。最后查背部。

slides.title: What lung sounds tell you
slides.body:
SoundThink of
WheezesNarrow lower airways: asthma, COPD
CracklesFluid or collapse: pulmonary edema, pneumonia
StridorUpper airway narrowing: an emergency
Pleural rubIrritated pleura, sharp pain on breathing
Diminished / absentPneumothorax, hemothorax, severe asthma

Most often missed: the quiet chest. If you can see or hear breathing from across the room, there's a problem.
slides.say: Wheezes are musical sounds from narrowed lower airways, as in asthma or COPD. Crackles are fine popping sounds from fluid or collapsed air sacs, as in pulmonary edema or pneumonia. Stridor is a harsh, high sound from the upper airway, and it's an emergency. A pleural rub is a creaking sound with sharp pain on breathing. But the finding most often missed is the quiet one: breath sounds that are diminished or absent. That can mean a pneumothorax, blood in the chest, or asthma so severe that almost no air moves. A silent chest is not a calm chest.
slides.sayZh: 哮鸣音是下气道变窄发出的乐音样声音，见于哮喘或 COPD。湿啰音是细小的噼啪声，来自肺泡里的液体或肺泡塌陷，见于肺水肿或肺炎。喘鸣是上气道发出的刺耳高调音，属于急症。胸膜摩擦音是一种嘎吱声，伴随呼吸时的锐痛。但最常被漏掉的是「安静」：呼吸音减弱或消失。可能是气胸、胸腔积血，或者哮喘严重到几乎没有气体进出。安静的胸腔不等于平静的胸腔。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: SOB with asthma / COPD
slides.body:
BC protocol: Shortness of Breath with a history of asthma/COPD, plus the CPAP guideline.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Position of comfort, usually sitting forward
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94% (may not be reachable)
  • Auscultation
  • History and baseline vital signs
  • Salbutamol by nebulizer or MDI

PCP adds

  • Salbutamol with ipratropium (ipratropium: one dose)
  • IM epinephrine: SpO₂ < 90% and/or bronchospasm not settling
  • Consider dexamethasone
  • Consider CPAP: RR > 24 + SpO₂ < 94% on O₂ + accessory muscles
slides.say: Here's where your chest exam pays off. In the BC protocol for shortness of breath with asthma or COPD, every licence level positions the patient, gives oxygen aiming for ninety-four percent, listens to the chest, takes a history and baseline vitals, and gives salbutamol. The PCP adds more, and each step depends on your findings. Add ipratropium to the salbutamol, as a single dose. Consider intramuscular epinephrine when the saturation is under ninety, or moderate to severe bronchospasm hasn't settled with salbutamol. Consider dexamethasone. And consider CPAP when all three are present: breathing over twenty-four a minute, saturation under ninety-four on oxygen, and accessory muscle use.
slides.sayZh: 这里体现出胸部检查的价值。BC 的「哮喘/COPD 病史伴气短」流程里，所有级别都要：摆好体位、给氧目标百分之九十四、听诊胸部、问病史并测基线生命体征、给沙丁胺醇。PCP 多做的每一步都取决于你的检查发现：在沙丁胺醇里加异丙托溴铵，只给一次；血氧低于九十，或者中重度支气管痉挛用了沙丁胺醇还没缓解，考虑肌注肾上腺素；考虑地塞米松；三项同时具备时考虑 CPAP：呼吸每分钟超过二十四次、吸氧下血氧低于九十四、使用辅助呼吸肌。

slides.q: A 70-year-old with heart failure is very short of breath: RR 32, SpO₂ 89% on oxygen, accessory muscle use, crackles at both bases. Which extra finding rules out CPAP?
options: He is alert and follows commands
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A seventy-year-old with heart failure is very short of breath. He breathes thirty-two times a minute, his saturation is eighty-nine percent on oxygen, he's using accessory muscles, and you hear crackles at both lung bases. Which extra finding rules out CPAP? A, he is alert and follows commands. B, his blood pressure is eighty-four over fifty-two. C, his heart rate is one hundred twelve. D, both ankles are swollen. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位七十岁的心衰病人严重气短：呼吸每分钟三十二次，吸氧下血氧百分之八十九，在用辅助呼吸肌，两肺底都听到湿啰音。再加上哪一项发现，就不能用 CPAP？A 他清醒、能听从指令；B 血压八十四比五十二；C 心率一百一十二；D 双脚踝肿胀。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In the BC CPAP guideline, a systolic pressure under ninety is a contraindication, because the added pressure in the chest can lower the blood pressure further. A is actually required: the patient must be awake and following commands. C and D fit heart failure and don't rule CPAP out. That's why a PCP takes full vital signs, not just lung sounds, before choosing CPAP.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 的 CPAP 指引里，收缩压低于九十是禁忌证，因为胸腔内增加的压力会让血压进一步下降。A 其实是必需条件：病人必须清醒并能听从指令。C 和 D 都符合心衰的表现，不排除 CPAP。所以 PCP 在决定用 CPAP 之前要测全套生命体征，不能只听肺。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Your numbers now drive drugs: fit the cuff, pick the right arm
  • Know the patient's own normal before calling a value acute
  • Don't let one finding, like unequal pupils, make the diagnosis
  • New quiet side? Suspected pneumothorax rules out CPAP
  • New crackles during fluids: fluid may be backing into the lungs
  • Listen again after every treatment
slides.say: Now the new watch-outs. First, your numbers now drive drugs, so a badly fitted cuff can lead to a wrong decision. Second, know the patient's own normal: someone whose usual systolic is one hundred seventy may be in trouble at one hundred ten. Third, don't let one finding, like unequal pupils, make the diagnosis. Fourth, if one side of the chest goes quiet, think pneumothorax, and remember that a suspected pneumothorax is a contraindication to CPAP. Fifth, new crackles during a fluid bolus may mean fluid is backing up into the lungs. So listen again after every treatment.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲新的注意事项。第一，你的数字现在决定用药，袖带不合适可能导致错误决定。第二，要知道病人自己的正常值：平时收缩压一百七十的人，到一百一十可能就出问题了。第三，别让单一发现（比如瞳孔不等大）替你下诊断。第四，一侧胸部变安静，要想到气胸；记住疑似气胸是 CPAP 的禁忌证。第五，补液过程中出现新的湿啰音，可能是液体在往肺里倒灌。所以每次处置之后都要再听一次。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Lung auscultation: at least 6 anterior or 6 posterior points
  • The book says each lobe, front and back; BC sets a minimum
  • Spinal Management: follow NEXUS and the Canadian C-Spine rules
  • PCP only: the secondary survey adds a functional enquiry by system
slides.say: A few BC points for your exams. When you listen to the lungs, BC sets a minimum: at least six points on the front of the chest, or six on the back. The book just says to listen over each lobe, front and back, so practise a fixed six-point pattern. For the neck, the BC Spinal Management protocol tells every licence level to follow the NEXUS criteria and the Canadian C-Spine rules. And one PCP-only item: in the BC assessment model, the PCP's secondary survey adds a functional enquiry, questions organized by body system. We'll cover it in Chapter seventeen.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考点。听肺时 BC 有最低要求：前胸至少六个点，或后背至少六个点。书里只说每个肺叶前后都要听，所以要练熟一套固定的六点听诊。颈部方面，BC 的脊柱处理流程要求所有级别遵循 NEXUS 标准和加拿大颈椎规则。还有一项 PCP 独有：在 BC 评估模型里，PCP 的二次评估多了一项系统问诊（functional enquiry），也就是按身体系统组织的提问。我们在第十七章讲。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Vital signs are a trend; a true number needs the right cuff and arm
  2. Head, eyes, neck and skin give clues to the cause: acute or chronic?
  3. Full chest exam, 6+ points; findings drive CPAP and PCP drugs

Next: the heart, abdomen, limbs and nervous system
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: vital signs are a trend, and a true number needs the right cuff on the right arm. Two: the head, eyes, neck and skin give you clues to the cause, and part of your job is sorting chronic findings from acute ones. Three: do a complete chest exam with at least six listening points, and let your findings drive PCP decisions like CPAP, ipratropium and epinephrine. Next lesson, we finish the exam: the heart, the abdomen, the limbs and the nervous system. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，生命体征是趋势；要得到真实数字，袖带和手臂都要选对。二，头、眼、颈和皮肤给你病因的线索，你的工作之一是分清慢性和急性发现。三，做完整的胸部检查，至少听六个点，让你的发现来决定 PCP 的处置，比如 CPAP、异丙托溴铵和肾上腺素。下节课我们把体检做完：心脏、腹部、四肢和神经系统。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
